name: Gibraltar
prevalence_note: The Royal Gibraltar Police Economic Crime Unit has repeatedly published telephone-scam warnings after reports of callers pretending to be from a bank, including a later notice about people claiming to work for National Westminster Bank and asking for an online-banking one-time password. The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission has separately told the public that attempted frauds against people and firms in Gibraltar have increased, including callers who pose as a local bank or as the RGP.
cross_border_note: Gibraltar's public calling code is +350. Both the RGP and the GFSC warn that a number on the display can be spoofed so that it resembles a bank or a withheld line; the RGP has also described the practice as caller ID spoofing in the NatWest-related reports. A genuine follow-up should use a number already printed on a statement or a bank card, or the regulated-entities list on the GFSC site, not the inbound display.

scams.name: Spoofed bank call asking for an online-banking one-time password
scams.name_en: RGP Economic Crime Unit: telephone callers, including some claiming to be from NatWest, ask the person to log into online banking and read out the one-time password; the display may be spoofed
context_keywords: one-time password on a bank login

red_flag_keywords.text: confirm the OTP from your login
fraud on your account, log in now

scams.signals_en: Caller claims fraud on an account and tells the victim to open online banking and read out a one-time password. RGP notes caller ID can be spoofed to resemble a trusted bank, even when no losses were reported in that specific batch.
scams.legit_en: RGP notes banks already hold customer PINs, usernames, passwords and OTPs and will not phone to ask for them. To verify, end the call and contact the bank in person or via details on a card or official letter.
bait_tactics: End the call and ring the bank only on a number already printed on a card or a statement, not on the number that just appeared on the screen.
Say that a one-time password, PIN or login secret is never spoken to an unsolicited caller, even if the display looks like a bank.
Ask which branch or unit the person claims to represent, and offer to continue the matter only through the bank's own published channel.

scams.name: Caller posing as a local bank or the RGP who wants desktop control or a payment site
scams.name_en: GFSC consumer alert: fraudsters pose as local banks or the Royal Gibraltar Police, use the bank's number or a withheld line, and ask for personal details so they can control a desktop and start payments through a fake site
context_keywords: pose as the Royal Gibraltar Police

red_flag_keywords.text: install remote access on your computer
download Team Viewer so I can help
open this site to move the money
I am calling from the RGP about fraud

scams.signals_en: GFSC warns of local calls claiming the victim was defrauded and seeking details to take over their desktop and open a fake payment site. A separate RGP alert also warns against requests to install remote-access tools like TeamViewer.
scams.legit_en: Neither Gibraltar banks nor the RGP ask for logins, remote desktop control, or transfers on an unexpected call. GFSC advises ending the call and ringing back only via a statement or its regulated-entities register.
bait_tactics: Refuse any request to install a remote-access program or to open a site the caller dictates, and close the session if one has already been started.
Say that the Royal Gibraltar Police and the banks do not take desktop control in an inbound fraud call, and that the matter can be reported through the police's own published route.
Offer to walk into a branch or to use only the GFSC register or a printed bank number, after the present call has been ended.
